newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bonds jump, peseta strong before 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bonds jump, peseta strong before 97 budget.

text.p: Spanish bonds surged and the peseta remained strong on Friday, as financial markets continued to bank on the government delivering a tough 1997 budget that will shape up Spain's finances for Europe's single currency.
Spain's IBEX-35 share index dipped on profit-taking after two days of strong rises that carried it nearly two percent higher.

At 1050 GMT, just one hour before the presentation of initial information on the accounts, the Spanish 10-year benchmark bond was up 115.05, yielding 7.81 percent, compared with 114.10 or 7.93 percent at Thursday's close.

Since the end of August, the IBEX index has risen to 4,203.48 from 4,025.47. Spanish bond futures prices have soared more than six full points this month, while yields on the 10-year benchmark bond have dropped sixty basis points.
The peseta continues its battle to break through 84.00 marks, and dealers say the only thing checking it given bond strength is the Bank of Spain buying marks for pesetas.

"The market has discounted the best of all possible scenarios, but in any case the feeling is still optimistic and it's even possible we will see further gains after the document is presented," a bond trader said.
The government has pledged to cut the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from the 4.4 percent projected for this year.
The market expects the austere accounts to enable the Bank of Spain to lower its key money market rate for the sixth time this year at its next regular repo tender on October 3.
The interest rate is now at 7.25 percent, down from nine percent at the beginning of the year.

Economy Ministry Rodrigo Rato is set to present basic economic forecasts underlying the 1997 budget at a short news conference at 1145 GMT. Budget details will be made available on Monday, following presentation of the draft to parliament.
